change_summary: Added a shadow-mode viability runner that checks whether the accepted A+B stack produces enough true collision days to support a collision-day tie-break alpha experiment.
hypothesis: On rare true cohort-competition days, a collision-aware tie-break driven by candidate cohort composition can improve marginal slot allocation more stably than rejected broad day-state sleeve routing.
notes: Result: across the three fixed windows there was only 1 true collision day, 0 collision days with any entries, and 0 mixed-strategy collision days with entries. This makes the proposed collision-day tie-break currently untestable rather than rejected on performance. The next alpha candidate should pivot away from slot-collision toward a fresh mechanism with repeated triggered exposure, likely the observed trend_instant_failure family noted in exp-20260426-001.
